title: Digital Marketing — Beginner to Advanced
short_description: A practical digital marketing course that starts at what a funnel is and ends with a complete campaign you can show a client. No marketing background needed.
description:
Most digital marketing courses teach you where the buttons are. Buttons move. This one teaches the reasoning underneath them, then puts you in the tool to do the work.

You start with the fundamentals — what digital marketing is, who you are selling to, and how a funnel, a persona and a KPI relate. Then you build: a landing page, an SEO audit, a content calendar, a social strategy, a Meta Ads structure, a Google Search campaign, a YouTube growth plan, an email programme, a WhatsApp funnel, a GA4 dashboard and a conversion test.

The advanced half covers what the field has actually added lately: influencer and affiliate programmes, e-commerce, generative AI in marketing work, answer and generative engine optimisation for AI search, marketing automation, and the strategy layer that decides where the budget goes.

It closes with the part that gets you hired: a career and freelancing module, and a capstone where you run one fictional brand through every channel in the course and present the result as a KPI and ROI report.

Every module is roughly 30% theory and 70% practical. You finish each one with a worksheet or template you filled in, a lab you worked through, and an assignment marked against a published rubric. All case studies use fictional brands, so nothing here invents data about a real company.

faqs.question: Do I need marketing experience to take the Digital Marketing course?
faqs.answer: No. The course starts at what digital marketing is and builds from there. It is written for college students, MBA students, freshers, career changers, entrepreneurs and freelancers, and it defines every term the first time it appears.

faqs.question: How long does the Digital Marketing course take to finish?
faqs.answer: There is a suggested sixteen-week plan at roughly eight to ten hours a week, which includes the labs and assignments. The course is self-paced, so you can move faster or slower, and your progress is saved if you stop and come back.

faqs.question: Is the Digital Marketing course really free?
faqs.answer: Yes. Every lesson, lab, worksheet and assignment is free once you create an account. The first three lessons are readable without an account at all.

faqs.question: Do I need to pay for Semrush, Ahrefs or other paid marketing tools?
faqs.answer: No. The labs are written so they can be completed with free tools, and where a paid tool is the industry standard we explain what it does and what the free alternative gives up. Tool pricing and free tiers change often, so check the current terms before you rely on any of them.

faqs.question: Does the Digital Marketing course include coding?
faqs.answer: Only where a marketer genuinely needs it. Module 2 has a HTML and CSS landing page, module 3 has JSON-LD schema markup, module 11 has spreadsheet formulas for ROI, ROAS, CAC and LTV, module 15 has prompt templates with optional Python, and module 17 has automation blueprints and webhooks. Each one comes with starter code, a hint, a full solution and the expected output.

faqs.question: What is the Digital Marketing capstone project?
faqs.answer: You pick one fictional brand and take it through everything in the course: market research, a persona, a competitor analysis, a landing page, an SEO and content strategy, a social calendar, Meta and Google Ads campaigns, an email campaign, analytics, a dashboard, a budget, and a final KPI and ROI report you present. It is the piece of work you show an employer or a first client.

faqs.question: What certificate do I get from the Digital Marketing course?
faqs.answer: There are five completion levels, from Beginner through to Capstone, each earned by finishing the modules it covers. These are completion certificates from this platform. They are not Google, Meta or HubSpot certifications, and nothing in the course should be read as implying otherwise.

faqs.question: Will the Digital Marketing course get me a job or guarantee results?
faqs.answer: No course can promise that, and we do not. What this one gives you is a portfolio of finished work, a capstone you can present, and a career module covering the roles, proposals, pricing and client reporting that the job actually involves. The hiring, the ranking and the revenue depend on your market and your effort.

faqs.question: Do the brands used in the Digital Marketing examples exist?
faqs.answer: No, and that is deliberate. Every case study uses one of four fictional brands — a D2C skincare brand, a local dental clinic, a B2B SaaS tool and an online course seller — so no example invents data or performance figures about a real company.

faqs.question: How does this differ from the Generative AI for Beginners course?
faqs.answer: They overlap by one module and otherwise sit side by side. Generative AI for Beginners teaches how the models work and how to build with them. This course teaches marketing, and module 15 covers the slice of AI a marketer uses day to day. You can take either first.
